intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-booked budget train or bus transfer toward Poschiavo. The Bernina Express or regional trains via Tirano connect to Poschiavo. Check into B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama, settle in, and get a good night's rest.

meals.lunch: On the flight or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick sandwich or snack at the airport or train station convenience store (CHF 8-12) before heading to the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your train ticket from the airport to Poschiavo in advance via SBB.ch for the best budget fares. The journey from Zurich takes approximately 4-5 hours via Chur and St. Moritz on the Rhaetian Railway. Keep luggage light for easier train travel. Confirm hotel late check-in arrangements before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Explore the charming village of Poschiavo on foot — visit the historic Piazza Comunale, the Collegiate Church of San Vittore, and the colorful Italianate-style buildings that reflect the region's unique Swiss-Italian heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo), just a short walk or free bus ride from the village center. Walk along the lakeside promenade enjoying stunning winter mountain views. Visit the small local Museo della Valposchiavo (free or minimal entry fee) to learn about the valley's culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the village in the early evening. Explore local shops for budget groceries for snacks. Relax at the B&B and plan your ski days ahead. Early bedtime to prepare for an active week.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh bread, local cheese, and cured meats from a local Poschiavo deli or Co-op supermarket (CHF 8-12) and enjoy a picnic near the lake
meals.dinner: Osteria La Cruna in Poschiavo — a cozy local restaurant offering traditional Grigioni cuisine. Try pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) or polenta dishes (CHF 15-22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to help recover from jet lag and travel fatigue. Poschiavo sits at about 1,014m elevation — take it easy to acclimatize. The village has a distinctly Italian character despite being in Switzerland, making it a unique and budget-friendly base.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Bernina Express train from Poschiavo toward Pontresina or Samedan (approximately 45-60 min, CHF 15-20 one way with Swiss Travel Pass discount). Head to Corviglia Ski Area above St. Moritz — one of the most accessible ski resorts from Poschiavo. Purchase a budget half-day ski pass (afternoon) or look for discounted beginner/off-peak passes (CHF 50-65 for a day pass). Rent ski equipment at local rental shops in Pontresina for better rates than on-mountain rentals (CHF 30-45/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the beginner to intermediate slopes of Corviglia. The area offers excellent groomed runs with panoramic Engadin Valley views. Take ski lifts up to around 3,000m for breathtaking Alpine panoramas. Focus on enjoying the mountains without overextending your budget — stick to included lift zones.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Warm up with a hot chocolate or glühwein at a local café. Rest tired muscles at the B&B.

meals.lunch: Pack a DIY lunch from the Co-op the night before — sandwiches, fruit, and energy bars (CHF 5-8). Eating on the mountain is very expensive.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or soup using groceries from the local supermarket in the B&B kitchen if available, or visit a local Poschiavo pizzeria for a budget pizza (CHF 14-18)

day_by_day.notes: Book ski rental equipment in advance from Pontresina rental shops (Pontresina Sport or similar) for the best rates. Avoid renting directly at St. Moritz resort which is significantly more expensive. Check SBB.ch for regional rail passes that cover the Bernina line — a Swiss Travel Pass or Engadin regional day pass can save significant money across the week.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train northward to Diavolezza Ski Area (alight at Bernina Diavolezza station — only 20-25 min from Poschiavo, CHF 8-10 each way). Diavolezza is one of Switzerland's most spectacular glacier ski areas at 3,000m+. Purchase a morning ski pass (CHF 45-58 for half-day). Ski the famous Diavolezza glacier run with views of Piz Palü and Morteratsch Glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza or hike the free snowshoeing trail near the Morteratsch Glacier (just one stop further on the train). The Morteratsch Glacier trail is FREE and one of the most stunning winter walks in Switzerland — a 2km marked trail through snow-covered forest to the glacier's edge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Visit the local thermal area or simply relax. Prepare a warm meal at the B&B if kitchen facilities are available.

meals.lunch: Pre-packed sandwiches and thermos of hot tea/coffee from B&B (CHF 0-5). There is a mountain restaurant at Diavolezza but it is expensive — avoid it.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Albrici in Poschiavo — a historic restaurant in the village with local Valposchiavo specialties. Budget-friendly set menus available (CHF 18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza is arguably the most spectacular ski destination accessible from Poschiavo and is a must-do. The Morteratsch Glacier walk is completely free and absolutely unmissable — one of the most accessible glacier experiences in the Alps. Dress in warm layers as temperatures at 3,000m can drop to -15°C or below in February.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in and enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast. Walk to the Poschiavo Valley floor for snowshoeing on marked free trails around the lake and valley. Rent snowshoes locally for approximately CHF 15-20/day if you don't have your own — far cheaper than skiing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short bus or walk to Miralago village at the southern end of Lake Poschiavo. Enjoy the peaceful winter scenery and photograph the frozen or partially frozen lake surrounded by Alpine peaks. Visit the small local chapel. Walk back along the lakeside trail (approximately 4km, free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village. Browse the weekly local market if available. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the B&B. Consider a budget-friendly fondue night — buy fondue mix and bread from the Co-op (CHF 10-15 for two people) and enjoy it at the B&B.

meals.lunch: Co-op supermarket in Poschiavo — pick up local bread, Graubünden dried meat (Bündnerfleisch), local cheese, and fruit (CHF 10-14)
meals.dinner: DIY Swiss cheese fondue at the B&B using supermarket ingredients (CHF 10-15 total) — an authentic Swiss experience on a budget

day_by_day.notes: Day 5 is a deliberate rest and recovery day from intensive skiing. Snowshoeing around Poschiavo Valley is free or very low cost and equally rewarding. The lake walk between Poschiavo and Miralago is one of the region's hidden gems and rarely crowded. This is a great day to recharge before the final ski day.

day_by_day.morning: Final big ski day — take the Bernina Express to Pontresina and access Languard or Alp Languard ski and toboggan area (more budget-friendly than St. Moritz). Alternatively, return to Diavolezza for a second day of glacier skiing if conditions were excellent. Purchase a morning half-day pass (CHF 35-50) to save money. Focus on runs not yet completed.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, explore Pontresina village — a charming Engadin village with free walking trails, historic tower houses, and the Chapel of Santa Maria with medieval frescoes (free entry). Walk the Roseg Valley trail (flat, easy, free) through snow-covered forest — a classic Engadin winter walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Celebratory final evening dinner in the village. Pack bags and prepare for departure the next day.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch from B&B or Co-op as before (CHF 5-8)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for a farewell dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — try Pizzeria-Ristorante Il Borgo or Osteria La Cruna for a traditional Grigioni meal with local wine (CHF 22-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can be busier on the slopes — head up early (first lift at 8:30am) to avoid crowds and get the best snow conditions. The Roseg Valley walk in Pontresina is completely free and one of the most beautiful cross-country skiing and walking areas in the Engadin — horse-drawn sleigh rides are available but optional (CHF 25-35/person). Confirm your departure logistics for Day 7.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely B&B breakfast. Check out of the hotel. Take a final morning stroll through Poschiavo village and pick up local souvenirs — Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart), local honey, or Graubünden dried meats from the village shops (budget CHF 15-25 for gifts). Take photos of the village and valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Bernina Express or regional train toward Tirano (Italy) or Chur/Zurich depending on your departure route. The Bernina Express ride itself is a UNESCO World Heritage railway journey — enjoy the spectacular mountain scenery as a final free experience. Transfer to your departure airport (Zurich approx. 4-5 hours, Milan Malpensa approx. 2-3 hours via Tirano).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible budget Alpine adventure in one of Switzerland's most authentic and least touristy mountain valleys.

meals.lunch: Pack remaining groceries for the train journey, or buy a sandwich at Tirano or Chur train station (CHF 8-12)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight home

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Poschiavo to Tirano or Chur is itself a world-class scenic railway experience and is included in most Swiss Travel Passes — it's a perfect free finale to the trip. Book your return train tickets in advance on SBB.ch. Budget summary for the week: Accommodation (6 nights B&B approx. CHF 70-90/night = CHF 420-540), ski passes (3 days approx. CHF 130-180), ski rental (2-3 days approx. CHF 80-120), food (approx. CHF 25-35/day = CHF 175-245), transport (approx. CHF 80-120 with regional passes). Estimated total: CHF 885-1,205 (approximately USD 980-1,340) for the week excluding flights.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Check in, settle into your room, and get a good night's rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama around 23:30–midnight after transfer. Grab a light snack if available at the B&B, unpack, and rest up for the week ahead.

meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport or convenience store en route to Poschiavo. Keep it simple — grab a sandwich or Swiss chocolate bar for the road.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. Poschiavo is roughly 2–2.5 hours from Zurich Airport via car/train. Confirm late check-in arrangements with the B&B ahead of time. The Bernina Pass road may have winter conditions — verify road status or opt for the Rhaetian Railway (Bernina Express route) if driving is not preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast with panoramic Alpine views. Take a gentle orientation walk around the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the frozen Lake Poschiavo shoreline. This eases you into the Alpine environment at altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Livigno ski area (approx. 45–60 min drive via the Forcola di Livigno pass, subject to winter road conditions — check road status). Livigno is a duty-free ski resort with excellent beginner-to-intermediate slopes. Purchase a half-day lift pass and enjoy your first ski session of the trip on well-groomed pistes. Rent equipment on-site if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Stroll the village and warm up with a vin brûlé (mulled wine) at a local café before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — expect fresh bread, local cheese, cold cuts, yogurt, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the Livigno slopes — try a hearty bowl of minestrone soup and a panino. Budget CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or La Rösa in Poschiavo — enjoy local Graubünden specialties like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) and a glass of Valtellina red wine. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Verify Forcola di Livigno pass road conditions before driving — an alternative is to take a taxi or organized shuttle. Livigno lift passes cost approximately CHF 45–55 for a half-day. Bring your passport as Livigno is technically in Italy (duty-free zone). Dress in layers and apply high-SPF sunscreen — Alpine UV is intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Livigno ski resort. Depart from Poschiavo after breakfast with a full-day lift pass. Start your morning on the Carosello 3000 sector — wide, well-groomed blue and red runs perfect for warming up. The slopes offer stunning views of the surrounding Rhaetian Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Mottolino sector for more challenging red and black runs. Consider a ski lesson with a local instructor if you want to sharpen your technique (book in advance, approx. CHF 60–80/hour). Take a mid-afternoon break at a slope-side rifugio for a hot drink and snack.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening — after returning to the Poschiavo area, seek out a cozy local restaurant offering traditional Swiss cheese fondue. This aligns perfectly with the available 'Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening' experience. Enjoy a pot of classic moitié-moitié (Gruyère and Vacherin) fondue with crusty bread, cornichons, and local white wine. A quintessential Alpine après-ski experience.

meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Livigno — try the local specialty sciatt (cheese-filled buckwheat fritters) or a plate of pasta at a rifugio. Budget CHF 20–35.
meals.dinner: Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant or arranged fondue experience. Budget CHF 40–55 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day Livigno lift pass costs approximately CHF 55–65. Livigno has over 115km of ski runs suitable for all levels. The duty-free status makes après-ski drinks and equipment purchases notably cheaper than elsewhere in Switzerland. Book fondue dinner in advance as mountain restaurants fill up quickly in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour — depart Poschiavo early by train (Rhaetian Railway from Poschiavo/Tirano direction, connecting via Chur or St. Moritz toward Interlaken). This is a long but spectacular journey. Board the cogwheel train from Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and 360-degree panoramic views of the Bernese Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Jungfraujoch plateau — visit the Ice Palace (carved tunnels inside the glacier), the Sphinx Terrace viewpoint, and the Snow Fun Park where you can try short sledding runs and snow activities. Spend 2–3 hours at the top before descending back toward Grindelwald or Interlaken for a brief afternoon stop.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Poschiavo via train — it will be a long travel day (total round-trip is approximately 8–10 hours including transfers). Arrive back at the B&B by evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner in Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure — pack snacks for the train journey.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant or self-service restaurant at Jungfraujoch — expect Swiss mountain cuisine (rösti, soup, hot chocolate). Budget CHF 30–45 at altitude.
meals.dinner: Simple, comforting dinner back in Poschiavo — try Osteria Suisse for local pasta or risotto dishes. Budget CHF 30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch round-trip ticket costs approximately CHF 145–210 depending on your Swiss Travel Pass or rail discount card — book in advance online for savings. The journey from Poschiavo is long; consider an overnight stay in Interlaken or Grindelwald if you prefer, or treat this as an immersive full-day rail adventure. Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454m — ascend slowly and stay hydrated. Dress in full winter gear as temperatures at the top can be -15°C or colder.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari — depart Poschiavo by train toward Zermatt (approximately 3–3.5 hours via St. Moritz and Chur, or via Brig). Zermatt is car-free, so the train journey is part of the experience. Arrive and take in the iconic Matterhorn view. Begin your ski safari on Zermatt's legendary 360km of groomed pistes — start with the Sunnegga Paradise sector on beginner-friendly blues and cruisy reds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari into the Klein Matterhorn sector — take the cable car to 3,883m for Europe's highest ski area. Ski the long, scenic runs back down through Trockener Steg. The views of the Matterhorn from the slopes are absolutely breathtaking and unmissable.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Zermatt's famous après-ski scene — visit the Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub for a lively atmosphere and cold beer. Dinner in Zermatt before taking the evening train back to Poschiavo (or consider a one-night stay in Zermatt to avoid the long return journey — budget hotels available from CHF 120–180/night).

meals.lunch: Slope-side lunch at a Zermatt mountain restaurant — try rösti with a fried egg or a hearty goulash soup. Budget CHF 30–45.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Zermatt at Restaurant Whymper-Stube — known for hearty Swiss mountain food and great atmosphere. Try the raclette or Valais-style meat dishes. Budget CHF 45–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt lift passes cost approximately CHF 90–100 per day. The Ski Safari experience from the available options covers 360km of pistes — focus on 2–3 sectors to make the most of the day. Book lift passes online in advance for small discounts. If returning same day, check last train times from Zermatt carefully. A one-night stay in Zermatt is recommended to fully enjoy the resort without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail — travel from Poschiavo toward Davos (approximately 1.5–2 hours by Rhaetian Railway via Filisur or Landquart). Davos is the highest city in Europe and home to over 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails. Rent classic or skate-ski equipment at a local rental shop and begin your cross-country adventure on the scenic Flüela Valley or Davos Lake trails — flat to gently rolling terrain ideal for all fitness levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the Nordic trails — the Dischma Valley route is particularly beautiful with mountain panoramas and quiet forest sections. Take a mid-afternoon break at a trailside hut for warm drinks and Bündner Nusstorte (walnut tart). If energy allows, try the slightly more challenging Sertig Valley loop.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Davos town briefly — visit the main promenade and browse local shops. Enjoy dinner in Davos before returning to Poschiavo by evening train.

meals.lunch: Packed lunch or trail hut stop — pick up fresh sandwiches and snacks from a Davos bakery in the morning. Budget CHF 15–20.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Belvédère or Bistro Schneider in Davos — try the Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef) platter and a warming Engadiner barley soup. Budget CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Davos Nordic trail pass costs approximately CHF 15–25 per day. Cross-country ski rental is approximately CHF 25–35. The Rhaetian Railway journey itself is a UNESCO World Heritage experience — enjoy the dramatic viaducts and mountain scenery. Davos can be busy on weekends — arrive early to secure rental equipment. Dress in breathable, moisture-wicking layers for Nordic skiing as you generate significant body heat.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo — enjoy a relaxed last B&B breakfast with Alpine views. Take a peaceful farewell walk along the shores of frozen Lake Poschiavo and through the village. Visit the local market if running on Sundays, or browse the Poschiavo Museum for a glimpse into local Romansh culture and history. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — local cheese, Bündner Nusstorte, or Swiss chocolate.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional half-day activity: gentle snowshoeing on marked trails around Poschiavo — rent snowshoes locally (CHF 15–20) and explore the pristine winter landscape at your own pace. Alternatively, visit the nearby Val Poschiavo for a scenic winter drive or train ride on the Bernina Express route — one of the world's most beautiful railway journeys passing over the famous Brusio spiral viaduct.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo — celebrate a wonderful week in the Swiss Alps with a special meal. Pack your bags and prepare for departure the following day.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast — savor it as your last Alpine morning meal.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local Poschiavo café — try a Capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings in cream sauce, a Graubünden specialty) or a simple cheese and meat platter. Budget CHF 20–30.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the best restaurant in Poschiavo — Ristorante Suisse or Al Cervo. Order the full Graubünden tasting menu if available: Bündnerfleisch, barley soup, venison or lamb main, and a local dessert. Pair with a bottle of Pinot Noir from the Graubünden region. Budget CHF 50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check B&B checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for afternoon activities. The Bernina Express (Poschiavo to Tirano or St. Moritz) is a must-do if time allows — even a short segment is spectacular. Confirm any onward travel arrangements for departure day. Exchange any remaining Swiss Francs or settle final bills. Swiss tipping etiquette: rounding up the bill or leaving 5–10% is appreciated but not mandatory.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Transfer from airport to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama via private luxury transfer service. Settle into your panoramic alpine suite and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the host.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled due to arrival time.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival at 22:30. Private chauffeur transfer to Poschiavo (~1.5–2 hrs depending on departure airport). Light welcome snack or room service upon check-in. Rest and acclimatize to the alpine altitude.

meals.lunch: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or a pre-arranged late-night charcuterie and cheese board with local Valposchiavo wines waiting in your room upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) in advance. Confirm check-in time with B&B Berninapass. Pack layers — Poschiavo sits at ~1,000m elevation and February nights are cold. Ensure ski gear is either shipped ahead or rental is pre-booked for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the B&B taking in the sweeping panoramic views of the Bernina Pass and surrounding peaks. After breakfast, take the scenic Bernina Express (or private car) up toward St. Moritz / Pontresina area (~40 min) for a morning ski session at Corviglia or Diavolezza ski area — both world-class resorts easily accessible from Poschiavo. Rent premium Völkl or Rossignol demo skis at the resort ski shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza (2,978m), renowned for its glacier runs and breathtaking Bernina massif views. Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant with panoramic terrace views. Optional: take the cable car to the summit for dramatic 360° alpine photography.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Freshen up at the B&B. Head into the charming village of Poschiavo for a premium dinner at one of the local fine-dining establishments, sampling Graubünden regional cuisine including pizzoccheri pasta, venison, and locally produced Poschiavo wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss alpine breakfast at B&B Berninahaus — fresh bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, soft-boiled eggs, homemade jams, and hot coffee or herbal teas.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Diavolezza Restaurant — try the Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), rösti with smoked salmon, and a glass of local Graubünden Pinot Noir.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse or Albergo Croce Federale in Poschiavo village — regional Graubünden specialties, local game, and an extensive Swiss wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book ski lift passes online in advance for Diavolezza/Lagalb ski area to avoid queues. Consider hiring a private ski instructor for the day if needed. Diavolezza is approximately 35 km from Poschiavo via the Bernina Pass road — confirm road conditions in February as the Bernina Pass may require snow chains.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast and depart for Zermatt by private luxury transfer or scenic train via St. Moritz → Chur → Visp → Zermatt (approximately 4–5 hours by rail, one of Switzerland's most scenic rail journeys). Arrive in Zermatt by midday. Check into a day-use arrangement or luggage storage at a luxury hotel such as The Omnia or Mont Cervin Palace. Begin the **Zermatt Ski Safari** — access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari with a private mountain guide. Ski the legendary Klein Matterhorn sector (3,883m — highest ski area in the Alps), the Schwarzsee runs, and the Gornergrat slopes. Pause for a gourmet lunch at a high-altitude restaurant with direct Matterhorn views. Explore the Italian border ski area of Cervinia if conditions permit.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski drinks at the iconic Zermatt Vernissage Bar or Papperla Pub. Dinner at a premium Zermatt restaurant. Overnight stay in Zermatt at a luxury property (upgrade from B&B for this night is strongly recommended).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at B&B before departure, or grab a premium pastry and coffee at St. Moritz train station café.
meals.lunch: Gourmet mountain lunch at Restaurant Findlerhof (3-star recommended, Michelin-recognized) or Chez Vrony in Findeln — raclette, truffle risotto, and locally sourced alpine dishes with Matterhorn views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See (legendary Zermatt mountain restaurant, advance reservation essential) or Restaurant After Seven — seasonal tasting menus with Swiss and French Alpine influences.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a car-free village — all transport within the village is by electric taxi or horse-drawn carriage. Book the Zermatt Ski Safari guide in advance through Zermatt Guides (zermatt.ch). The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car to 3,883m is a must-do. Dress in premium technical ski layers — temperatures at altitude can drop to -15°C or below.

day_by_day.morning: Full second day in Zermatt. Morning ski session on the Rothorn sector — less crowded and offering superb long red and black runs. Join the **Verbier Freeride Experience** preparation with a certified IFMGA mountain guide who will brief you on off-piste technique and safety (avalanche transceiver fitting, probe and shovel orientation). Morning warm-up on groomed pistes before venturing off-piste.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by private transfer or Glacier Express rail segment toward Verbier area (via Visp → Martigny → Le Châble cable car to Verbier, approx. 2–2.5 hours). Arrive in Verbier for an afternoon **guided off-piste freeride session** — explore Verbier's legendary off-piste terrain including the Col des Gentianes, Lac des Vaux, and the iconic Vallon d'Arbi freeride zones. Suitable for advanced intermediate to expert skiers.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at Farinet Bar or Pub Mont Fort in Verbier — world-famous après-ski scene. Dinner at a premium Verbier restaurant. Overnight in Verbier at a luxury chalet hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full luxury breakfast at Zermatt hotel — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, artisan breads, fresh-squeezed juices, and barista coffee.
meals.lunch: Quick mountain lunch at Verbier's La Chaux restaurant or Cabane Mont Fort (2,457m) — hearty alpine fare including cheese fondue, tartiflette, and hot chocolate.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Carrefour Restaurant inside Hotel Rosalp, Verbier (one of Switzerland's most celebrated restaurants, advance reservation essential) — refined French-Swiss cuisine with exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride Experience requires a minimum intermediate-advanced ski level. Avalanche safety equipment (ABS airbag pack, transceiver, probe, shovel) is provided by the guide service but personal rental is available. Verbier is part of the 4 Vallées ski domain with 410km of marked runs. Book accommodation in Verbier in advance — W Verbier or Chalet Carlotta are excellent luxury options.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Verbier — optional final ski run or snowshoe tour through the Verbier forest trails. Check out and transfer by private luxury vehicle or train toward Interlaken / Grindelwald area (approx. 2.5–3 hours via Martigny → Spiez → Interlaken). Arrive in the Jungfrau Region by late morning. Check into luxury accommodation such as Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa in Interlaken or Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof in Grindelwald.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the legendary **Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Tour** — take the cogwheel train from Grindelwald or Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace (carved entirely from glacial ice), the Sphinx Observatory, the Aletsch Glacier (UNESCO World Heritage Site), and enjoy panoramic views of four countries on a clear day. Allow 4–5 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.evening: Descend by cogwheel train back to Grindelwald or Interlaken by late afternoon. Spa and wellness session at the hotel's luxury spa facilities — perfect recovery after days of skiing. Dinner at a premium Interlaken or Grindelwald restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Verbier hotel before departure — continental spread with Swiss cheeses, cold cuts, fresh fruits, and pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch summit — dine at the Crystal Restaurant (3,454m altitude) or the self-service Top of Europe Restaurant — enjoy hot meals with arguably the most spectacular dining view in Switzerland.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Lauberhorn inside the Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof, Grindelwald, or La Terrasse at Victoria-Jungfrau Grand Hotel — classic Swiss fine dining with Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau mountain views.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially in peak February season. The journey from Interlaken Ost takes approximately 2 hours each way. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at 3,454m — stay hydrated and ascend slowly. Temperatures at the summit average -10°C to -20°C in February — bring an extra warm layer regardless of base clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning ski session at First ski area in Grindelwald — access via the First Gondola. Enjoy spectacular runs with views of the Eiger North Face. Optional: try the First Flyer zipline or First Cliff Walk by Tissot (weather permitting in February). Advanced skiers can tackle the challenging runs beneath the Schreckhorn and Finsteraarhorn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel by scenic Golden Pass train or private transfer toward Davos (approximately 3–4 hours via Interlaken → Spiez → Chur → Davos). Arrive in Davos by mid-afternoon. Check into luxury accommodation at Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvédère or Intercontinental Davos. Begin the **Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail** experience — glide through the first section of 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails in the highest city in Europe (1,560m). The Flüela and Sertig valleys offer spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Davos town center. Enjoy a traditional **Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening** — warm up after a day in the snow with a classic Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy Davos mountain restaurant. Pair with crisp Swiss white wine (Fendant from Valais is traditional) and finish with a pear schnapps (Williams).

meals.breakfast: Full alpine breakfast at Grindelwald hotel — freshly baked Zopf bread, local mountain cheeses, bircher muesli, and hot beverages.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bergrestaurant Bort (mid-station, First area) — rösti, Bündner Nusstorte, and warming soups with Eiger views.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at Restaurant Flüela Stübli or Landhaus Restaurant in Davos — traditional Gruyère and Appenzeller cheese fondue, raclette, and Swiss charcuterie board in an authentic alpine chalet setting.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski equipment (classic or skate) can be rented at the Davos Nordic Center. The Davos Parsenn ski area (connected to Klosters) is also world-class if you prefer downhill skiing in the afternoon. Davos hosts the World Economic Forum annually — the town has excellent infrastructure and premium services year-round. Pre-book the fondue restaurant as weekends fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — leisurely breakfast at the Davos hotel. Optional morning Nordic ski session on the Davos trails or a relaxing spa morning at the hotel wellness center. Pack and check out. Begin the scenic return journey toward Poschiavo and the B&B Berninahaus via private transfer or train through the Engadin valley (Davos → Filisur → Tirano direction via Albula/Bernina Railway — a UNESCO World Heritage rail route).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama by early afternoon. Enjoy a final afternoon at leisure — take a gentle snowshoe walk in the Val Poschiavo, visit the historic village of Poschiavo with its Romansh architecture and Spanish Quarter (unique to this valley), or simply relax on the panoramic terrace with a glass of local wine and take in the Bernina massif views one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury dinner in Poschiavo — celebrate the end of an extraordinary alpine week with a premium dinner at the best local restaurant. Reflect on the week's experiences over a curated Swiss wine flight. Early night in preparation for departure or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at Steigenberger or Intercontinental Davos — full buffet with hot and cold stations, freshly made omelettes, smoked fish, artisan cheeses, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch en route — stop at Pontresina or St. Moritz for a final upscale lunch at Hanselmann Konditorei (St. Moritz institution since 1894) — exquisite pastries, light lunches, and the best hot chocolate in the Engadin.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Albergo Croce Federale or Ristorante La Scala in Poschiavo — savoring the best of Valposchiavo cuisine: local trout, polenta with mountain cheese, Brusitt (local braised meat specialty), and Poschiavo dessert wines.

day_by_day.notes: The Albula/Bernina Railway route from Davos back toward Poschiavo is itself a UNESCO World Heritage experience — book a panoramic window seat. If departure flight is the following day, arrange a private transfer to Zurich (3.5 hrs), Geneva (4 hrs), or Milan Malpensa (2 hrs) airport for the morning. Confirm all luggage logistics with the B&B host. Consider purchasing local Poschiavo wines, Bündner Nusstorte, and Swiss chocolates as premium gifts before departure.
